elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — cap runs to both HDI and the Company; no retained language leaves either party uncapped (deterministic check "no unlimited Customer liability language remains" passes).

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: "the greater of (i) the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and (ii) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000)" — correct basis ("fees paid or payable", not broader "all amounts"), correct temporal anchor (preceding the claim), correct floor amount.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect or consequential damages" — expressly bilateral.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "Excluded Claims" (carved out of the cap) "means a Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations...".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include "its breach of its data protection or security obligations".
Excluded Claims include "its indemnification obligations"; opening words "Except for Excluded Claims" place them outside the cap.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include "its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights".

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: "The Company's payment obligations under this Agreement are not damages subject to the foregoing cap." The Company (Deerskin, the fee-paying customer) is our party, and the carve-out covers payment obligations as a whole rather than a narrow defined Fees subset.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed" — bilateral.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Cap floor/basis includes "the fees paid or payable by the Company ... in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim"; the USD 1,000,000 alternative is a floor in Customer's favour, not a substitution below 12 months' fees.
Excluded Claims (outside the cap) include "its indemnification obligations".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include "a Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations".

reasons: The document genuinely lacks any limitation-of-liability, aggregate cap or damages-exclusion language (Sections 1–5, 8, 9, 10 are silent; 10.2 addresses only no-joint-venture), so treating the rule as 'missing' and inserting a clause is appropriate.

All eleven preferred elements are satisfied by the single inserted passage: mutual cap, greater-of formula with 'fees paid or payable' and a USD 1,000,000 floor, lookback tied to the 12 months preceding the claim, mutual indirect/consequential exclusion, uncapped Excluded Claims covering confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and the other Party's IP, plus an unqualified Customer-payment carve-out.

Minimality holds: the change is a pure insertion after Section 9(b) with no deletions or paraphrase of surrounding text, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural boilerplate, no extra damages categories, and no duplication — each sentence maps to a checklist element.

Intent is preserved: 'Excluded Claims' is defined in the inserted text itself, no cross-reference dangles, the Globix acknowledgement and mutual representations in Section 9 survive intact, and nothing contradicts the fee, term or site-management mechanics elsewhere.

Drafting note only (not a defect): the insertion sits in the Warranties section rather than a standalone liability article, and the lookback runs from 'the claim' rather than 'the event giving rise to the claim' — both are consistent with the element text and the detection guidance, but the drafter may prefer a discrete Section 9(c) heading for clarity.
